items.titleEn: Precious metals tumble despite falling yields as Hormuz tensions intensify - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Thursday, as renewed Middle East tensions sent crude oil prices higher, reinforcing inflation concerns and expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. A sharp selloff in technology shares and falling Treasury yields failed to generate sustained safe-haven demand for bullion, while silver faced additional pressure from concerns about industrial demand and slowing economic activity. At the time of the latest verified late-afternoon reading, spot gold was trading near $4,021.20 an ounce, down $119.10, or 2.88%, while spot silver was trading near $54.440, down $3.410, or 5.90%. Market positioning remains divided between persistent inflation pressure, weaker economic activity and growing financial-market instability. September consumer inflation increased 0.6% on the month and 3.7% annually , while producer prices rose 1.3% and 6.3%, respectively . Fed funds futures continue to favor no change at the Oct. 27-28 Federal Reserve meeting, with recent pricing indicating approximately an 84% probability of a pause and a 16% probability of a 25-basis-point increase. December tightening remains the central market expectation, although the precise probabilities have fluctuated as traders reassess growth risks and the inflationary impact of elevated energy prices. Treasury yields declined Thursday as selling in technology shares encouraged demand for government bonds. However, falling yields failed to support gold, suggesting that precious metals positioning, liquidation pressure and the outlook for further monetary tightening remained dominant considerations.

items.titleEn: War in Iran, higher energy prices are only delaying gold's rally to $5,000; mining stocks remain undervalued – Gabelli
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The ongoing war in Iran and disruptions to global energy supplies are driving inflation pressures higher, forcing central banks to maintain restrictive monetary policies, which is taking its toll on gold ; however, one fund manager says the conflict is only delaying gold's eventual rally, while the mining sector continues to generate significant cash flow at historically elevated prices. In an interview with Kitco News, Chris Mancini, co-portfolio manager of the Gabelli Gold Fund (GOLDX), said that if the conflict in Iran and disruptions to oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz had been resolved during the summer, gold prices would probably already be trading at $5,000 an ounce. Mancini explained that the conflict has created a difficult environment for gold as higher energy prices fuel inflation, raising expectations that the Federal Reserve will continue increasing interest rates.

items.titleEn: Newmont beats third-quarter earnings expectations as higher gold sales boost profits; miner raises 2026 cost outlook
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Despite ongoing headwinds, the world's largest gold producer reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings Thursday, as higher gold sales volumes and elevated metal prices helped boost profitability and cash flow. Thursday after the North American equity close, Newmont Corporation (NYSE: NEM) reported adjusted net income of $2.20 per diluted share for the third quarter of 2026, beating analysts' consensus estimate of $1.94 per share by $0.26, or 13.4%. The results also exceeded the high end of analysts' earnings estimates, which ranged from $1.78 to $2.19 per share. Adjusted earnings increased 28.7% compared with $1.71 per share reported in the same quarter last year.

‘Very bizarre action' as gold retraces entire summer rally to test $4,000/oz: AI weakness, or yen intervention? – Jesse Columbo
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold’s dramatic Thursday selloff Has erased all of the yellow metals gains since the summer, and the lack of correlation with the US dollar index and bond yields suggests that this could be more than liquidations from the tech selloff, and may indicate the next round of yen interventions by the U.S. government, according to Jesse Colombo, independent precious metals analyst and founder of the BubbleBubble Report. Columbo told Kitco News on Thursday afternoon that he was just trying to decipher what was going on in the gold market. “Very bizarre action,” he said. “The dollar index is down. Normally you would expect the dollar index to be up one percent on a day like this, and yet it's down 15 basis points.”
